caption:
Every Ethereum address starts with 0x because it's written in hexadecimal: base 16, digits 0–9 and A–F. Two hex digits make one byte, so an address is 40 hex characters, 20 bytes 🧙

Day 3 of learning crypto security from zero.

Free cheat sheet: 10 crypto hacks explained. Link in bio.

#learntocode #hexadecimal #ethereum #smartcontracts #web3security #codingjourney

scenes.say: Every Ethereum address starts with *zero x*. Here's what that means.

lines: 0 to 9, then *A B C D E F*
scenes.say: Zero x means *hexadecimal*, base sixteen. After nine, you count with letters: A is ten, up to F, *fifteen*.
Same trick as binary, with sixteens. One zero is *sixteen*. F F is *two fifty five*, one full byte.

scenes.sub: hex characters = *20 bytes*. Add the 0x and you get 42.
scenes.say: Two hex digits make one byte. So an address is *forty* hex characters: twenty bytes.

lines: Compiled contracts are bytes, shown in *hex*
scenes.say: Contract bytecode is shown in hex too. Most Solidity contracts start with *six zero eight zero*.
Hex is just counting with sixteen digits. Follow the journey.
